text:
incident-bot: PAGER: Sev2 - Autoscale capacity shortfall detected on gpu-pool-us-west. Errors increasing for generation routes, queue depth rising. Paging #eng-oncall @channel — runbook: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/autoscale-capacity

Alex: acked. I'm oncall. quick status: which routes impacted and rough customer impact?

Maria: seeing spikes on /v1/generate and /v1/chat. 5xx rate up ~6% last 8m. Queue depth (generation-queue-usw) moved from 20 -> 750 between 1959990700 and 1959991100. Latency p50/p95 jumped: p50 120ms -> 890ms, p95 1.8s -> 8.2s. GPU pool occupancy = 100% (all nodes in use). HPA target CPU 60% but CPU on workers ~95%. Warmup success rate low (~12%).

Simon: adding what I see from autoscaler events: ops-runner-bot posted repeated backpressure: "failed to provision node: quota exceeded" around 1959991002 and 1959991020. HPA attempted scale up but underlying cloud API returned 429/insufficient_quota. That explains why HPA couldn't clear queue.

Jess: confirmed customer reports from internal tracker: 3 enterprise customers reported degraded responses; no full downtime yet but errors for long requests.

Maria: logs snippet for warmup attempts:
```
2026-05-12T12:31:02Z warmup-manager INFO warmup request queued model=redwood-xl instance_id=pool-usw-12
2026-05-12T12:31:18Z warmup-worker ERROR failed to attach model: OOM during load, retrying
2026-05-12T12:31:50Z warmup-manager WARN retry exhausted for instance pool-usw-12, marking unhealthy
```

Simon: hypothesis tracking (brief):
- H1: Cloud quota limits prevented additional GPU nodes -> HPA scale attempts failed -> queue backlog.
- H2: Warmup latency + retries caused effective capacity to be lower; many instances failed warmup and were marked unhealthy.
- H3: Rapid queue growth + conservative HPA cooldown prevented proactive scaling (scale-up rate limit).

Alex: mitigation plan (live):
1) Short-term: increase HPA minReplicas to 6 and temporarily raise scaleUpLimit if possible. If cloud quota blocks, fall back to reassign lower-priority workloads to other pools.
2) Kick off targeted warmup on idle nodes that can take model (avoid OOM targets).
3) Customer comms: notify impacted customers with ETA ~30-60m until queue drains or fallback model enabled.

Jess: taking 1). Running command now:
```
kubectl patch hpa generation-hpa -n redwood -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":6}}'
kubectl annotate nodepool gpu-us-west allow-emergency-scale=true
```

Jess: status: patch accepted, HPA now minReplicas=6. autoscaler attempted new nodes at 1959991187. Cloud API responded: quota limit still blocking creation: "quotaExceeded.gpus": true.

Maria: trying warmup workaround: prefetch shards to smaller subset to avoid OOM. Running warmup CLI: `./infra-cli warmup --pool gpu-us-west --instances 4 --model redwood-xl --prefetch=safe`

Priya: ops-runner-bot output (events):
```
1959991002 autoscaler ERROR failed_create NodeGroup: insufficientQuota: GCE quota gpus us-west-1 exceeded
1959991020 autoscaler WARN backoff scaling suppressed due to repeated failures
1959991190 autoscaler INFO attempted scale: desired=8 actual=6
```

Simon: quick workaround suggestion: 1) temporarily route low-priority/large-gen traffic to a smaller-but-compatible model (redwood-lg) to reduce warmup pressure; 2) enable model fallback in routing policy for next 45m.

Alex: do 1) and 2). Maria, can you apply routing policy and watch latency for fallbacks?

Maria: applied routing override to send requests >8k tokens to redwood-lg at 1959991252. Observed immediate drop in queue growth rate slope. p95 for fallback route ~1.1s.

Jess: ops update: cloud quota team notified, request for temporary quota bump opened (ticket INC-4523). ETA unknown but flagged high.

Alex: timeline quick notes for RCA (putting in-thread):
- 1959990700: small queue growth starts after a big customer batch job.
- 1959990950: warmup errors begin appearing (OOM during load).
- 1959991002: autoscaler failed_create (quotaExceeded).
- 1959991025: HPA attempted scale but cooldowns + provisioning delays => backlog increases.
- 1959991187: mitigation minReplicas=6 applied, cloud blocked node creation.
- 1959991252: routing fallback enabled to redwood-lg; queue growth slows.

Simon: collecting logs for RCA. What I need: kube events for autoscaler (kubectl get events -n redwood --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp), warmup manager logs, and infracli provisioning logs. I'll assemble timeline + raw events. Assigning to myself to produce preliminary RCA doc.

Alex: responsibilities:
- Maria: own mitigation until handoff (monitoring + warmup attempts)
- Simon: collect logs and draft RCA (timeline, hypothesis validation, required infra changes)
- Jess: continue customer comms + cloud quota escalation
- Priya: prepare runbook note to add cloud quota checks to smoke tests

Jess: customer comms sent (status update) at 1959991320.

Maria: warmup prefetch reports: 3/4 instances warmed successfully; one instance failed and marked unhealthy -> now effective warmed instances = 3. Queue decreased from 750 -> 220 by 1959991400. Error rate down to 1.2%.

Simon: snapshot command I ran for records: 
```
kubectl get hpa generation-hpa -n redwood -o yaml > /tmp/hpa-gen-1959991325.yaml
curl 'https://metrics.internal/dashboards/queue?start=1959990600&end=1959991420' -o /tmp/queue-metrics.json
```

Alex: handing off to night shift now. Current state: mitigations applied (routing fallback, HPA min bumped, warmup prefetch), queue trending down but still above baseline. Ongoing blockers: cloud quota for new GPUs. Next oncall: Jess (night) — handoff at 1959991457.

Jess: ack. I'll watch for regressions and coordinate with infra for quota. I'll follow up in #eng-infra. Leaving this thread visible for RCA collection. :thumbsup:
